chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated from Ibn Muskan from Abu Hilal al-Razi who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man appointed an agent to divorce his wife when she became menstruating and when she became pure. The man left, and then it occurred to him, so he testified that he had annulled what he had ordered him to do, and that it had occurred to him regarding that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him inform his family and let him inform the agent.'
ai.seo_question: How does a husband revoke a delegated divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural requirements for revoking a conditional delegated divorce (*tawkil*), emphasizing that mere internal change of mind is insufficient without explicit notification to both the agent and the family. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that legal agency relies on clear communication of authority changes to prevent ambiguity in marital status. The ruling underscores the importance of transparency in family law matters, ensuring all parties are aware of the revocation before the agent executes the divorce.
